day_shape: 89 items dominated by the announced US-Iran MoU (Araghchi/Pezeshkian say signing Friday in Switzerland), E4+17-nation leaders' statement and UN SG welcoming the deal, Trump pledging Strait of Hormuz "completely opened" Friday, Israeli political/security pushback, and continued IDF strikes in south Lebanon.

threads.label: US-Iran MoU signing set for Friday
threads.summary: Iranian FM Araghchi and President Pezeshkian said on regime channels that a US-Iran memorandum of understanding will likely be signed Friday in Switzerland, framing it as a victory delivered within Khamenei's red lines. Iran International reported Iranian media split between hardline denunciation and pro-diplomacy framing.

threads.label: International welcome for the deal
threads.summary: The UK, France, Germany and 14 other governments issued a joint E4 leaders' statement welcoming the US-Iran peace deal, and UN Secretary-General Guterres issued a statement of welcome. Oman's foreign minister called it "a victory for diplomacy" and Times of Israel reported world leaders welcoming the deal as Trump heads to the G7.

threads.label: Israeli pushback on Iran deal
threads.summary: Netanyahu told a press conference he and Trump don't always "see eye to eye," and Jerusalem Post reported IDF and Mossad officials warning the nuclear deal is insufficient. Former PM Bennett said the "clock for regime change in Iran" starts when Israel's government changes; Times of Israel framed the October 7 wars as over with Israel uncertain on next steps.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz reopening logistics
threads.summary: Trump said in Evian-les-Bains alongside Macron that the Strait of Hormuz will be "completely opened" on Friday. Times of Israel and Jerusalem Post reported experts and shippers saying mine-clearance and confidence rebuilding could take weeks, while oil prices fell and stocks rose on the framework announcement.

threads.label: Lebanon front continues despite deal
threads.summary: Times of Israel correspondent Mannie Fabian reported one killed in an Israeli drone strike on a car in Kfar Tebnit, south Lebanon, and Times of Israel reported Israel vowing to stay in south Lebanon and respond "with full force" to any Iranian strike. Defa Press and Hezbollah claimed Hezbollah fired Kornet missiles at advancing Israeli troops near Kfar Tebnit and framed the MoU as covering Lebanon.

threads.label: Khamenei and regime victory framing
threads.summary: Khamenei's office posted a message declaring Iranians "the definitive victors of the third imposed war" and warning of enemy plans to sow internal division. IRIB, Defa Press, Quds Force commander Qaani, judiciary chief Ejei and the army spokesman amplified the victory narrative; Hamas and Hezbollah issued statements congratulating Tehran.

threads.label: Iran at the World Cup in Los Angeles
threads.summary: Jerusalem Post and Times of Israel reported the Iranian national team arrived in the US for its first World Cup match in Los Angeles, with protests planned by the Iranian diaspora against Tehran and the recent US war. Iranian Americans were reported split between watch parties and demonstrations outside the stadium.

events.title: The IDF says it struck and killed two Hamas operatives who posed a threat to troops in the Gaza Strip earlier today. A strike in central Gaza killed Saleh Khalifa, a cell commander in Hamas's Nuseirat Battalion, and strike in the Strip's north killed Muhammad al-Habil, a cell commander in Hamas's West Jabalia Battalion, according to the military. The IDF says the pair had been planning attacks on troops, "posed an imminent threat," and were then killed in "precise strikes."

events.title: Following a fresh assessment, the IDF Home Front Command is lifting the nationwide gathering restrictions imposed yesterday amid fears of Iranian missile fire. "As part of the changes, it was decided to remove the restriction on gatherings of up to 5,000 people in all regions of the country," the military says. In communities on the northern border there are no changes to the current guidelines, which restrict gatherings to 100 people outdoors and 400 indoors.

events.title: Lebanese media reports that an car driving in the southern Lebanon town of Kfar Tebnit was hit in an Israeli drone strike this morning. "Injuries were reported," Lebanon's National News Agency says. NNA also reports that Israeli artillery shelling hit Kfar Tebnit and the nearby town of Nabatieh al-Fawqa. There is no immediate comment from the IDF. Israeli officials have not yet commented on the ceasefire between the US and Iran, which supposedly also includes ending the fighting in Lebanon.
